Reframing the September 18, 2019 FOMC statement through the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) points to a more cautious read than a purely macro take. The July 2019 SLOOS indicates banks tightened standards and other terms on C&I loans and on construction and land development loans, with weaker demand in the latter. While some banks reported willingness to lend in certain consumer categories and largely unchanged demand/standards for other consumer loans, there was also tightening in “other consumer” segments. A few reports of easier construction standards appear outweighed by the broader net tightening and weaker demand signals. Together, these results suggest business credit conditions were becoming less accommodative, aligning with the FOMC’s concerns about soft business investment and external headwinds, and reinforcing the case for data‑dependent easing and operational steps to keep markets functioning smoothly.

Bottom line: still supported by a strong labor market and policy accommodation, but tighter bank lending standards—especially for businesses and CRE—tilt the balance more guarded than before.
